CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFHTTP

CFHTTP makes your template a Web browser. It requests a URL, and the response ends up in the CFHTTP structure: the page text, the MIME type, the status code and the headers. It can also save the response to a file or turn a comma-delimited text file into a query.

Category

Internet protocols

Syntax

<CFHTTP URL="hostname"
    METHOD="GET/POST"
    USERNAME="username"
    PASSWORD="password"
    NAME="queryname"
    COLUMNS="column_names"
    PATH="path"
    FILE="filename"
    DELIMITER="character"
    TEXTQUALIFIER="character"
    RESOLVEURL="Yes/No"
    PROXYSERVER="hostname"
    PROXYPORT="port_number"
    PORT="port_number"
    USERAGENT="user_agent"
    REDIRECT="Yes/No"
    TIMEOUT="seconds"
    THROWONERROR="Yes/No"
    CHECKCERTIFICATE="Yes/No">
  CFHTTPPARAM tags (for POST)
</CFHTTP>

Attributes

URL
Required. Full URL to request, starting with http:// or https://. A user:password@ in the URL is used for Basic authentication when USERNAME is not given.
METHOD
Optional, default "GET". GET or POST. Use POST to send CFHTTPPARAM form fields and files.
USERNAME
Optional. User name for Basic authentication.
PASSWORD
Optional. Password for Basic authentication.
NAME
Optional. Turns the response into a query of this name. The response must be delimited text; the first row supplies the column names unless COLUMNS is given.
COLUMNS
Optional. Comma-separated column names for the NAME query.
DELIMITER
Optional, default ",". Field delimiter for the NAME query.
TEXTQUALIFIER
Optional, default double quote. Character that surrounds fields containing the delimiter.
PATH
Optional. Directory in which to save the response.
FILE
Optional. File name for PATH. Defaults to the last part of the URL.
RESOLVEURL
Optional, default "No". Yes rewrites relative HREF, SRC, ACTION and BACKGROUND links in an HTML response into absolute URLs, so the page still works when you display it from your server.
PROXYSERVER
Optional. Proxy server to go through. https:// requests are tunneled through it with CONNECT.
PROXYPORT
Optional, default "80". Port of the proxy server.
PORT
Optional, default "80" (443 for https). Port of the Web server, if it is not in the URL.
USERAGENT
Optional, default "KoldFusion". Value of the User-Agent header.
REDIRECT
Optional, default "Yes". Yes follows up to four redirects (301, 302, 303, 307). No returns the redirect itself; its target is in CFHTTP.ResponseHeader.Location, and with THROWONERROR="Yes" the redirect throws an exception.
TIMEOUT
Optional, default "60". Seconds the whole request may take, from connecting to the last byte.
THROWONERROR
Optional, default "No". Yes throws an Application exception when the server cannot be reached or answers with a status of 400 or higher.
CHECKCERTIFICATE
Optional, default from the Administrator ("Yes"). A KoldFusion extra. Yes checks an https:// server's certificate against the system's certificate authorities; No accepts any certificate.

Usage

After the call these variables are available:

Variable Contents
CFHTTP.FileContent The body of the response
CFHTTP.MimeType The MIME type, for example text/html
CFHTTP.StatusCode The status, for example "200 OK"
CFHTTP.Header All response headers as one string
CFHTTP.ResponseHeader A structure of headers, plus Status_Code, Explanation and HTTP_Version

Without THROWONERROR, a server that cannot be reached is not an error: FileContent is "Connection Failure" and StatusCode says the code is unavailable. Check for that, or use THROWONERROR="Yes" with CFTRY.

CFHTTP speaks HTTP/1.1 and understands chunked responses. For https:// URLs it needs the OpenSSL libraries on the server (KoldFusion loads them when first needed); without them the request fails with a "secure HTTP is not available" message. The server's certificate must be signed by a certificate authority the system trusts, or be this KoldFusion server's own certificate; otherwise you get "Connection Failure: the SSL certificate presented by ... could not be verified". Use CHECKCERTIFICATE="No", or clear "Verify server certificates in CFHTTP" on the Web Server and SSL page of the Administrator, to accept any certificate, as 1999 browsers mostly did.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- Fetch the documentation home page from this very server --->
<CFSET Scheme = "http">
<CFIF CGI.HTTPS IS "on"><CFSET Scheme = "https"></CFIF>
<CFSET Target = "#Scheme#://127.0.0.1:#CGI.SERVER_PORT#/CFDOCS/index.cfm">
<CFTRY>
  <CFHTTP URL="#Target#" METHOD="GET" TIMEOUT="10" THROWONERROR="Yes"></CFHTTP>
  <CFSET Start = FindNoCase("<TITLE>", CFHTTP.FileContent)>
  <CFSET Stop = FindNoCase("</TITLE>", CFHTTP.FileContent)>
  <CFSET PageTitle = "(none)">
  <CFIF Start GT 0 AND Stop GT Start>
    <CFSET PageTitle = Mid(CFHTTP.FileContent, Start + 7, Stop - Start - 7)>
  </CFIF>
  <CFOUTPUT>
  <TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
  <TR><TD>URL</TD><TD>#Target#</TD></TR>
  <TR><TD>StatusCode</TD><TD>#CFHTTP.StatusCode#</TD></TR>
  <TR><TD>MimeType</TD><TD>#CFHTTP.MimeType#</TD></TR>
  <TR><TD>Length</TD><TD>#Len(CFHTTP.FileContent)# characters</TD></TR>
  <TR><TD>Title</TD><TD>#HTMLEditFormat(PageTitle)#</TD></TR>
  </TABLE>
  </CFOUTPUT>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Application">
    <CFOUTPUT>
    <P><B>Could not fetch #Target#.</B><BR>#CFCATCH.Detail#</P>
    <P>(Is the KoldFusion server listening? Busy signal on the modem?)</P>
    </CFOUTPUT>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
